## S1R8-B01 — the section boundary was parsed out of a line with no Markdown block context (repaired at R9, recorded here at R11)

**This entry is late, and the lateness is part of what it repairs.** The R9 revision repaired `S1R8-B01` and shipped no ledger section for it, while the manifest continued to assert that the change ledger records this revision's repairs "in full". Measured over the R9 subject `208d0cacef94182d68f3f21c3e307e035b05540ccaa6b484b8ba54d6da5a041c`, the ledger was byte-identical to the R8 subject's at `0def6a5ab6106768345d3895638802aa067955f79c7f8dbb1cbed932a7d32ade`, contained the string `S1R8` zero times, `R9` zero times and `fenced_line_flags` zero times. The R10 Spec review blocked on that as `S1R10-B02`. **The repair described below is the R9 revision's work; only this record is R11's**, and it is written from the R9 mechanism as it stands in these bytes plus the coordinator's own replay against the R8 subject, not from the R9 handoff's account of itself.

Both R8 independent reviews returned `REQUEST_CHANGES` over subject `deb16e5ca3a7d4726733d9a2956c9aa1bdb8808f75844fbe21fc7c4ebb913e6c` (14 files, 486,204 bytes) on the shared identifier `S1R8-B01`. Those two verdicts stand over their own bytes and are not superseded here.

**Old.** `section_after_marker` decided "is this line an ATX heading?" by matching `^ {0,3}#{1,6}` against a line **in isolation**, with no Markdown block context. A `#` line is a heading only where Markdown is reading text; inside a fenced code block GFM renders content and no section boundary at all. One omission, both signs. A fenced example carrying a `## ` line ended §3.3 four lines into it, so a second class table placed behind that fence declared a seventh `bus_statement` leading terminal with the whole suite green at `EXIT=0`. On a truthful document the same omission reversed: a legitimate fenced example between the marker and the genuine table left an empty region, and the table a reader plainly sees was reported as "section 3.3 carries no class table" — a false red.

**New.** `fenced_line_flags(text)` computes one flag per line over the **whole document**, because fence state is a property of the document and not of the slice being read: a fence opened before the marker governs the lines after it. An opening fence is three or more backticks or three or more tildes at up to three spaces of indentation; a backtick fence may carry no backtick in its info string; a fence closes only on a run of the **same** character at least as long as the opening one and carrying no info string; an unclosed fence runs to the end of the document. Both heading scans consult it, and nothing else does: the region's **bytes** are untouched, so `class_rows` still reads every line of the region whatever it renders as. The enclosing-level default is `0`, which no ATX heading satisfies, so an undecidable level reads to the end of the document rather than to the nearest excuse to stop.

**Rationale — two designs were compared before either was written.** *(A)* suppress fenced **content** from the region, so a table behind a fence is simply not there. *(B)* leave the region's bytes alone and consult the fence state only where a heading is **recognized**. (A) closes every fixture in the fence family and reopens `S1R6-B01` in the same stroke: a row naming a class inside §3.3 is a defect **whatever it renders as**, which is the property `class_rows` exists to enforce, and (A) would make "render it as code" a way to hide a declaration again. (B) is the smaller change and the one that keeps the two obligations separable — what a line *means* is decided where it always was, and only what a line *is for section-boundary purposes* consults the new state. (B) was taken. Nothing here adds a verb, a production, a lattice, a refusal code, an authority or a subsystem, and `gaia-mission-room-protocol-v0.2.ebnf` is byte-identical at `a52a4141c6ab7777c8033df7e091ee40d591fe497bc8ddbac591cc5cef11342a`.

**Verification.** Red before green, replayed by the R11 coordinator rather than quoted. The shape is a legitimate-looking backtick fence carrying a `## ` line appended at `spec-v0.2:129`, followed by a second class table declaring a seventh `bus_statement` leading terminal `promote` beside a **Count** of 7 — spec 70,245 bytes, SHA-256 `0d19e01787ec03b9ee401da00363784f0391318402d431d63e3095363d61e65f`, identical bytes applied to both subjects. Over the **R8 subject** `deb16e5c…`, running that subject's own validator, all three §3.3 checks report `PASS` and both `SPEC_CLASS_COUNTS_MATCH_GRAMMAR` and `SPEC_CLASS_TERMINALS_MATCH_GRAMMAR` print `bus 6` while the document declares seven; over **these bytes** both report `FAIL  section 3.3 carries a row for bus_statement outside the class table`. The shape adds four lines, so `LEDGER_ANCHORS_RESOLVE` fails on **both** sides for ten shifted citations; detection is therefore reported as the state of the §3.3 checks and never as the run's exit code, which is the convention this ledger already uses (R6 Standards `S1R6-N04`). Six negative fixtures and four positive controls pin the family in the suite, taking it from 80 to 86 fixtures and from 5 to 9 controls: `NEG-R3B2-af` and `NEG-R3B2-ag` for backtick and tilde fences, `NEG-R3B2-ah` for a shorter inner fence that must not close the outer one, `NEG-R3B2-ai` for an undecidable enclosing level, `NEG-R3B2-ak` for an unclosed fence and `NEG-R3B2-aj` for the setext residual's direction; `POS-FENCE-a` and `POS-FENCE-b` are the false-red side on a truthful document, `POS-FENCE-c` holds §4 out of scope and `POS-FENCE-d` pins the unclosed-fence behaviour.

**What this does not establish.** This reader is not a CommonMark implementation and does not claim to be. It decides fences at **document level** only: a fence inside a block quote or a list item, an HTML block, and a setext heading are all outside what it reads. The setext consequence is pinned by `NEG-R3B2-aj` in the over-read direction and its converse — a legitimate class-naming row in a setext-headed §4 read as a §3.3 defect — remains an open residual. Everything the earlier sections left open stays open. It establishes no verdict, no acceptance, no freshness and no authority: **S1 remains `Pending`, M2–M7 remain `Absent`, and the bundle remains NOT INTEGRATED** until an independent reviewer binds these exact bytes. The R1–R8 verdicts each remain valid over their own subject and none is superseded.

## S1R10-B01 (Standards axis) — the §3.3 region parsed its ending boundary and hardcoded its start

The R10 Standards review returned `REQUEST_CHANGES` over subject `208d0cacef94182d68f3f21c3e307e035b05540ccaa6b484b8ba54d6da5a041c` on one blocker. **The two R10 axes number their blockers alike and mean different things**: the Standards `S1R10-B01` is this validator defect, the Spec `S1R10-B01` is a false statement in the manifest about its own bytes, and this ledger cites the axis with the identifier throughout. They are repaired as separate groups because they are separate defects in separate files.

**Old.** One proxy survived every round of this family. `section_after_marker(text, marker)` did `text.partition(marker)` and parsed only the **terminating** boundary out of the document. The region's **start** was the literal prose string `"mechanically witnessable over the whole protocol"` at `spec-v0.2:103`. Measured over the R9 bytes: §3.3 runs **9,991** characters from its heading at `spec-v0.2:95` to the line before `## 4.`, the region returned **9,547**, so **444 characters and eight lines — `spec-v0.2:95`–`102`** — were read by none of the three §3.3 checks. That prefix is ordinary normative prose, including the sentence `The only bus verbs are:` and the six-verb enumeration itself. `spec-v0.2:115` says a row naming a class **anywhere in §3.3** outside the table is a defect, and this ledger asserted in normative voice that "the section boundary is a property of the document, so it is parsed rather than approximated" — true of one end only. It is the same family one notch further out for the sixth consecutive round, and the R7 rebuttal recorded above condemns it in advance: a displaced **table** fails closed because its header is not found, and a displaced **row** is silent.

**New.** The one backward scan this reader already performed now decides both ends. It walked up from the marker, fence-aware, to the nearest ATX heading to read its **level** and discarded its **position**; keeping that position is the whole repair. `section_containing_marker(text, marker)` opens the region at that heading line and closes it exactly where R9 closed it. No heading text, no section number and no sentence is hardcoded: the marker still says *which* section this is — and the three checks still fail closed when it is absent, which is what keeps `spec-v0.2:103` a claim the suite reads rather than one it assumes — while the document says where that section starts and stops. With no enclosing heading decidable, the start is the document start and the end is the document end: undecidable fails open on the region and therefore closed on the check, in both directions, which is the direction the R9 repair already took at the other end. **(Superseded at R13.** "The marker still says *which* section this is" was not true of anything over these bytes: the marker sentence named no section, and *which* section was decided by proximity. The R12 Standards review reported that as `S1R12-B01`; the function is now `declared_section_region` and the marker sentence declares its own designator. This paragraph is left in place as the R11-era record it is.**)**

**Rationale — three designs were compared, two of them seriously.** *(A)* keep the position the existing scan already computes. *(B)* anchor on a literal heading string such as `"### 3.3 "`. *(C)* read to the end of the document. (B) is two lines and is immediately wrong for the reason under repair: a hardcoded literal standing in for a document property is exactly what the 2500-character window was and exactly what the marker sentence was, it breaks the moment the heading is reworded or renumbered, and it gives the region two readers — a string matcher for one end and a heading parser for the other — that can disagree. (C) catches every shape in the family and is refuted by the bundle's own declared scope: `spec-v0.2:115` says "anywhere in §3.3", not anywhere in the document, and `POS-FENCE-c` already requires a class table in §4 to be out of scope. (A) removes a literal rather than adding one, adds no new mechanism, and leaves one reader deciding both ends. (A) was taken. No positive check was added, so the count stays at 57; no normative prose was narrowed and **no specification byte was edited**, so the specification stands at 579 lines, `c6ae9a3ffa49c2ad9ee6e9ba0f0cd26480c7d14e5aa5fc3af54aad7bb5d3f0a9`, byte-identical to the R7, R8 and R9 candidates, and every line citation and load-bearing anchor in this file is undisturbed. `spec-v0.2:115` already claims exactly what the repaired reader now does, so the repair makes existing prose true rather than retreating to meet the code.

**Verification.** Red before green, over the exact bytes each side names. Detection is the state of the two §3.3 checks, not the exit code.

| Shape | Differs by | On the R9 bytes `208d0cac…` | On these bytes |
|---|---|---|---|
| the R10 reviewer's witness, replayed verbatim | one class row replacing the blank line at `spec-v0.2:102`, seventh terminal `promote`, **Count** 7; spec 70,098 B, `25ed3f37febc4928616bc2f8c548b4ddbadf98def9ff254fa3d74c0e26af958d` | both §3.3 checks `PASS`, printing `bus 6`; 57/0 positive, 86/0/0 fixtures, 9/0/0 controls, `VALIDATOR PASS`, `EXIT=0` | both `FAIL`: `carries a row for bus_statement outside the class table` |
| A/B control — the identical row two lines later | the same row at `spec-v0.2:104`, across the marker; spec 70,098 B, `613a3172c0c6686481e101b7f3fb91f07e4796b457a5ac9cb6278818cd103983` | both `FAIL` — so placement alone decided detection | both `FAIL`, unchanged |
| the whole-table form | a complete second class table in the prose prefix; spec 70,174 B, `b26435dcf711e1d4dd2d679a5ee27b972440a8589ab47bdf50db6d994b5fbf98` | both `PASS`, printing `bus 6` (the run is red on `BUS_TERMINALS_MATCH_SPEC` and `LEDGER_ANCHORS_RESOLVE` for unrelated reasons — the inserted header displaces the enumeration line and the shape adds three lines) | both `FAIL` |
| the truthful bytes | nothing | 57/0, 86/0/0, 9/0/0, `EXIT=0` | 57/0, 90/0/0, 11/0/0, `EXIT=0` |

**Four negative fixtures and two controls pin the family**, taking the suite from 86 to 90 fixtures and from 9 to 11 controls. `NEG-R3B2-al` is the reviewer's single-row witness; `NEG-R3B2-am` puts the same row on the first line of the section, the furthest point inside it from the marker; `NEG-R3B2-an` is the whole-table form, so a repair that reads a displaced row but not a displaced header cannot satisfy the family; `NEG-R3B2-ao` fences the §3.3 heading itself, so the enclosing heading becomes §3.2's and the region over-reads rather than under-reads. Against the R9 mechanism carrying this fixture set, **all four report "not caught"** and both controls stay clean, which is the red state this repair turns green. `POS-HEAD-a` is the load-bearing one: the identical seventh-verb table one heading earlier, in §3.2, **must not** trip, so design (C) catches every fixture above and fails here. `POS-HEAD-b` is a false-red guard and is recorded as one, not as a discriminator.

**What this does not establish.** One residual is **created** by this repair and is disclosed rather than hidden: the region now contains the §3.3 prose prefix, so `SPEC_ENUMERATES_ALL_CLASS_TERMINALS` — a subset test over code spans — can satisfy itself from the enumeration sentence at `spec-v0.2:99` as well as from the table cell. That widens what *that* check accepts. It removes no coverage, because a name dropped from the cell is caught by `SPEC_CLASS_TERMINALS_MATCH_GRAMMAR` in the dropped direction, which reads the cell and nothing else; but the widening is real and is recorded as such. The setext residual, the block-quoted and list-item fence residual, the HTML-block residual and the pipe-less degenerate-row residual are all unchanged and unaddressed. The `BUS_VERBS` / `LEDGER_TERMINALS` / `FRAME_TERMINALS` constants remain a third copy (`S1R4-N07`); a default run still does not hash the validator's own bytes (`S1R4-N02`); the two EBNF readers still disagree on nested comments; `COPYRIGHT_GATE_PRESERVED` still binds neither the text of the preserved notice, nor the pinned artifact digests, nor the eighteen upstream source identities (`S1R3-N04`). This revision touched none of them. It establishes no verdict, no acceptance, no freshness and no authority: **S1 remains `Pending`, M2–M7 remain `Absent`, and the bundle remains NOT INTEGRATED**. The R1–R10 verdicts each remain valid over their own subject and none is superseded.

## S1R10-B01 (Spec axis) — the manifest asserted a literal CRLF its own bytes did not contain

**Old.** Manifest §6 illustrated the Windows text-mode translation with a code span containing a **literal** CRLF, then asserted about itself: "this manifest contains one literal CRLF at the code span in this very section that illustrates the translation … by raw measurement this manifest is a mixed-ending file, and a reviewer measuring rather than classifying will see that." Measured over the R9 bytes that was false in both halves — the manifest contained **zero** CR bytes:

| Revision | manifest bytes | CRLF | bare LF |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| R7 | 11,796 | 1 | 115 |
| R8 | 12,462 | 1 | 115 |
| R9 (the reviewed subject) | 12,959 | **0** | 118 |

The property held at R7 and at R8; the R9 re-stamp normalized the CR away in a file that round did edit, undisclosed, and the rendered sentence degenerated to "text-mode stdout translates `\n` to `\n`" — a translation from LF to LF, which is the one thing that sentence exists not to say. Nothing mechanical catches it, because no check binds the manifest's self-description.

**New.** The bytes are pure LF and the prose describes the file as it is. The translation is illustrated with the escape sequences written as **text**, which is stable under any editor, normalizer or transport and needs no stray CR to say what it means. The nuance recorded as `S1R3-N05(b)` is now closed by construction rather than left open, and §6 says so and says which round closed it. The per-file census in §6 is restated from measurement: thirteen files carry LF only and zero CR bytes, and one file — `gaia-s1-r2-validator-output.txt` — carries CRLF, 210 of them and no bare LF, because it is captured by redirecting Python's stdout on Windows. **(Figure corrected at R13.** This paragraph and the Verification paragraph below both said `200` from R11 onward, against an R11 output file that measured 206 and an R11 manifest §6 that said 206. That is the Spec `S1R12-B01`, recorded in its own section below; the number here is now the one measured over the output file this bundle ships, and it is a different number again because this round adds three fixtures and one control and therefore four printed lines.**)**

**Rationale — two designs were compared.** *(A)* restore the literal CRLF, returning the file to one CRLF and making the existing paragraph true again. *(B)* keep the bytes pure LF and rewrite the paragraph. (A) re-arms an invariant that is a single stray CR byte, that no check can see, that no consumer preserves deliberately, and that an ordinary edit has now demonstrably normalized away once — that is how R9 lost it. Calling a fragile accident a property is what produced this blocker. (B) removes the fragile byte from the claim rather than the claim from the file, and there is no demonstrated requirement for mixed endings anywhere in the bundle: the validator's `read()` normalizes CRLF to LF before any text analysis, and every hash in manifest §2 and §3 is over raw bytes of the other files, so no check reads the manifest's line endings at all. (B) was taken. The change is stated as a change, with the round that caused it named.

**Verification.** Measurement, not mutation, on both sides — the claim under test is a statement about bytes, so the witness is the byte count itself. Over the R9 subject, `open(manifest,'rb').read().count(b'\r\n')` returns **0** against a paragraph asserting **1**, and `.count(b'\r')` returns 0. Over these bytes the same two measurements return **0** and **0**, against a paragraph that now asserts zero, and the file-by-file census in §6 is reproduced exactly by the same read across all fourteen files: thirteen at 0 CR, one — the captured output — at 210 CRLF and 0 bare LF (**`200` from R11 onward, corrected at R13 — see the Spec `S1R12-B01` section below**). No positive check changed, no fixture was added and none was removed, because there is no mechanism here to pin: the defect is a false sentence in an unbound file, and adding a check that binds a manifest's prose to its own bytes is a new mechanism well outside this round's scope. That is stated as a limitation immediately below rather than left for a reviewer to discover.

**What this does not establish.** Nothing mechanical now prevents this class of defect from recurring: the manifest is still the one artifact in the bundle whose self-description no check reads, and `--verify-manifest` still binds only the inventory rows — path, byte count and digest — of the other thirteen files. A future edit can make §6 false again exactly as R9 did, and only a reviewer measuring will see it. `S1R3-N05(b)` is closed as a *nuance* — the manifest is no longer a mixed-ending file — and is **not** closed as a *mechanism*. It establishes no verdict, no acceptance, no freshness and no authority: **S1 remains `Pending`, M2–M7 remain `Absent`, and the bundle remains NOT INTEGRATED**.

## S1R10-B02 — the manifest was re-stamped for R9 in five places and left carrying R8 claims in four others

**Old.** The R9 manifest edits were confined to the `**Revision:**` line, two inventory rows, §2's total, §3's four digests plus one sentence, and the validator description row. Four claims elsewhere were carried forward unedited and are false or materially incomplete over the R9 bytes, and a fifth was found by measurement here:

- **(a)** the preamble stated that "this revision repairs" `S1R7-B01` and `S1R7-B02` "**which the change ledger records in full**". Over those bytes "this revision" was R9, which repaired `S1R8-B01`; `S1R7-B01`/`B02` were repaired by R8; and the ledger recorded nothing about `S1R8-B01` at all.
- **(b)** §4's provenance row for `gaia-s1-r2-change-ledger.md` enumerated blockers only through `S1R7-B01..B02` and marked it **"no — new bytes"**. The bytes were not new: they were identical to a file both R8 lanes had reviewed, at `0def6a5a…`. The specification row likewise still credited "the R8 repair".
- **(c)** §7 enumerated the R1–R7 verdicts and concluded "**All seven subjects returned `REQUEST_CHANGES` on both axes**". There were eight reviewed subjects: the two independent R8 reviews over `deb16e5ca3a7d4726733d9a2956c9aa1bdb8808f75844fbe21fc7c4ebb913e6c` — the verdicts that authorized that very round — appeared nowhere. The preamble's lineage sentence had the same gap.
- **(d)** the ledger carried no `**Verification.**` paragraph for `S1R8-B01`, while (a) told a reviewer it did. The structural obstacle the R9 round cited is real and was reproduced: `LEDGER_NAMES_RESOLVE` hardcoded `if len(paras) != 15`, so a sixteenth paragraph failed the run unless the constant moved in the same edit. That obstacle does not explain the omission — the round already edited that file, so the coupled edit was one line — and the disclosure lived only in an out-of-bundle handoff, which is not one of the fourteen files a reviewer is told to bind.
- **(e)** found by measurement at R11, flagged by neither R10 lane: §5's reproduction recipe said `cd gaia-s1-r8-bundle-work-20260814T133934Z`, while the R9 subject was in fact assembled in `gaia-s1-r9-bundle-work-20260814T105100Z` — the manifest in the first directory measures 12,462 bytes at `1f05c524…`, the reviewed one 12,959 at `e11b5a73…`. A knowingly-stale directory name inside the section that tells a reviewer how to reproduce the fixed point is the same defect class as (a)–(c), and repairing (a)–(c) while leaving it would be indefensible.

**New.** All five are re-stamped for R11 over these bytes: the preamble names `S1R10-B01` on both axes and `S1R10-B02` as what this revision repairs, names the R10 entry subject `208d0cacef94182d68f3f21c3e307e035b05540ccaa6b484b8ba54d6da5a041c` and the R8 subject `deb16e5ca3a7d4726733d9a2956c9aa1bdb8808f75844fbe21fc7c4ebb913e6c` in the lineage list, and states what the ledger records without overstating it; §4's ledger row enumerates the groups this file actually contains and answers the "reviewed before?" column truthfully for each file; §7 enumerates the R8 **and** R10 verdicts alongside R1–R7 and states the correct subject count; §5 names the directory these bytes were assembled in. And **(d)** is closed by the four sections this ledger now carries, with the coupled expectation moved from a literal buried in a message to a named constant edited in the same commit as the sections it counts.

**Rationale — two designs were compared.** *(A)* write the missing ledger sections and move the coupled constant. *(B)* leave the ledger untouched and state in the manifest that the argument for these repairs deliberately lives in the validator docstrings and that the ledger carries no entry. (B) is simpler and does remove the false claim, and it was rejected: it makes the bundle's own convention — Old, New, Rationale with two designs compared, a red-then-green Verification, and What this does not establish, for **every** repaired blocker group since R1 — conditional on how much effort a round had left; it leaves a reviewer with no red-then-green table for the three most recent repairs; and a docstring cannot carry the measurements a Verification paragraph carries, so the in-bundle evidence would not be equivalent. (A) was taken. It is also the design that stops the ratchet: the obstacle in (d) recurs at every future round, and a named constant edited beside its own subject is one line instead of an argument.

**Verification.** Measurement over both subjects, since every claim here is a statement about text. Over the R9 subject the ledger contained `S1R8` 0 times, `R9` 0 times and `fenced_line_flags` 0 times, carried 15 `**Verification.**` paragraphs, and was byte-identical to the R8 subject's ledger at `0def6a5ab6106768345d3895638802aa067955f79c7f8dbb1cbed932a7d32ade`, 101,031 bytes; the manifest asserted seven reviewed subjects where there were eight, and named `S1R7-B01`/`B02` as what that revision repaired where it repaired `S1R8-B01`. Over these bytes the ledger carries 19 `**Verification.**` paragraphs — one per repaired blocker group, this sentence's own included — and the R8 and R10 subject digests, the R8 and R10 verdicts and the four blocker groups are each present in both the ledger and the manifest. The coupled constant was moved from 15 to 19 in the same edit: with the four sections added and the constant left at 15, `LEDGER_NAMES_RESOLVE` reports `FAIL … found 19` and the run exits 1, which is the red state, and with both moved the check reports `PASS` and `NO_DEBRIS` reports the same fourteen files. Every check name, fixture identifier and control identifier newly cited in this file resolves, which is what `LEDGER_NAMES_RESOLVE` decides on every run.

**What this does not establish.** The paragraph count is still a hardcoded number and is still disclosed as one: it is a claim about this ledger's shape that this ledger cannot make about itself, and a round that adds a section and forgets the constant fails closed — noisily, which is the safe direction, but it fails. Nothing binds the *content* of a Verification paragraph to the repair it names; a section could be written and be wrong, and only a reviewer reading it would see that. Nothing binds the manifest's prose to the manifest's bytes, which is the residual recorded under the Spec `S1R10-B01` above and is the mechanism by which (a)–(c) and (e) became possible in the first place. The two R8 verdicts and the two R10 verdicts are recorded here as standing facts about other subjects; **recording a verdict is not producing one**, this author expresses none, and none of them transfers to these bytes. It establishes no verdict, no acceptance, no freshness and no authority: **S1 remains `Pending`, M2–M7 remain `Absent`, and the bundle remains NOT INTEGRATED** until fresh independent Standards and Spec reviews both bind these exact bytes.

## S1R12-B01 (Standards axis) — the §3.3 region decided *which* section it read by proximity to a prose sentence

The R12 Standards review returned `REQUEST_CHANGES` over subject `596224b221e9463f49d04cb3909076c26ade0412d916c5f496d2c29e606fdb78` on one blocker, and the coordinator reproduced it independently before any edit was made. **The two R12 axes number their blockers alike and mean different things**, exactly as the two R10 axes did: the Standards `S1R12-B01` is this validator defect, the Spec `S1R12-B01` is a stale byte count in this file, and this ledger cites the axis with the identifier throughout. They are repaired as separate groups because they are separate defects in separate files.

**Old.** `section_containing_marker(text, marker)` walked up from the marker, fence-aware, to the **nearest** ATX heading of **any** level and opened the region there. The R11 docstring and the `S1R10-B01 (Standards axis)` section above both claimed "the marker still says *which* section this is, and the document says where it starts and stops". Over the R11 bytes the first half of that was true of nothing: the marker sentence named no section, so *which* section the region was got decided by **proximity** — whichever heading happened to be nearest above the marker — and proximity is a property an ordinary edit changes. One heading placed between the §3.3 heading at `spec-v0.2:95` and the marker at `spec-v0.2:103` moves the region's start down to it, and everything above it, still §3.3 to every reader of the document, is read by none of the three §3.3 checks. Three heading forms do it, and all three are legitimate Markdown a specification author would write:

- a **deeper subsection**, `#### 3.3.1`;
- a **same-level subsection**, `### 3.3.1` — which is this document's own house style, not a contrivance: `spec-v0.2:305` spells `### 7.1.1` at the same ATX level as `### 7.1` at `spec-v0.2:283`, so in this specification the *numbering* and not the *level* carries the nesting, and a level-climbing repair is wrong here before it is written;
- a **second heading for the same section**, `### 3.3` restated.

The witness is the seventh-verb row this family has used since R10, `| `bus_statement` | `promote`, … | 7 | …`, placed on the **first line of §3.3** — the `NEG-R3B2-am` position, which is caught there — with one of those headings on the blank line before the marker. Both edits replace a blank line, so the specification stays at **579** lines and no citation and no `LEDGER_ANCHORS` entry drifts. It is the same family one notch further out for the seventh consecutive round, and the failure mode is the one the R10 section above names and then commits: a *position* standing in for an *identity*.

**New.** The identity is read rather than inferred. `spec-v0.2:103` now declares the section its own control is scoped to — "and the scope of that witness is §3.3, the section whose heading stands above this sentence" — and `declared_section_region(text, marker)` takes the designator from the marker's **own line**, then resolves the **unique unfenced ATX heading whose text opens with that designator as a whole number**. `3.3` matches `### 3.3 Exactly six non-privileged verbs` and does not match `### 3.3.1` or `### 3.30`, because the designator must be followed by neither a digit nor a dot-digit; one trailing dot is admitted, so `### 3.3. Title` still resolves. A deeper subsection is therefore *inside* the region rather than the start of it, which is what a reader of `### 7.1.1` already assumes. Zero matching headings or two are refused rather than resolved by position — the rule `class_rows` already applies to two rows for one class — and the reason is returned to the caller and printed, instead of an empty region reaching `class_rows` and the run reporting "section 3.3 states no Count for `bus_statement`": a true failure with a misleading cause, which this bundle treats as its own defect class (`S1R3-N07`). The function's return type widens from `str` to `(region, problem)` for exactly that reason, and its name changes because "the section containing the marker" is no longer what it computes.

**The closing boundary is untouched, deliberately.** The forward scan still starts on the line *after* the marker and still stops at the first unfenced ATX heading of the declared heading's level or shallower — the same value, 3, on these bytes. Changing only the opening boundary is what leaves `POS-FENCE-c`, `POS-FENCE-d`, `NEG-R3B2-aj` and the whole closing family reading exactly the bytes they read before.

**This is a specification edit, and it is the only one.** One line changed in place, no line added, no line removed, no normative requirement narrowed, no verb, lattice, refusal code, authority or subsystem added or removed: the six non-privileged verbs `register`, `send`, `inbox`, `ack`, `heartbeat`, `handoff` are byte-identical, and `EXACTLY_SIX_BUS_VERBS`, `BUS_TERMINALS_MATCH_SPEC` and `NO_SEVENTH_VERB_PRODUCTION` all read the same six. The clause adds an anchor the document did not have; it removes nothing.

**Rationale — five designs were compared, three of them seriously.**

| | Design | Why not |
|---|---|---|
| **(A)** | climb the ATX ancestor chain to the shallowest enclosing heading | Opens the region at `## 3. Architectural split` or at the document title. `POS-HEAD-a` already requires a class table in §3.2 to be **out** of scope and §3.2 is inside §3, so this fails an existing control on the first shape. It is design (C) of the R10 section wearing a different hat. |
| **(B)** | climb exactly one level from the marker's enclosing heading | Closes the `#### 3.3.1` form and nothing else. Against `### 3.3.1` there is no strictly shallower heading before `## 3.`, so it either misses the shape or degenerates into (A) and fails `POS-HEAD-a`. It is also unsound *for this document*, where `### 7.1.1` sits at the same level as `### 7.1`: level does not encode nesting here. |
| **(C)** | derive the designator from the marker's *enclosing* heading and re-anchor at the first heading carrying it | Validator-only, no specification edit — the cheapest of the five. Rejected because it is still rooted in proximity: a decoy heading numbered `### 3.4` above the marker relocates the identity itself, and the mechanism then anchors confidently on the wrong section. It half-closes the family and reads as if it closed it. |
| **(D)** | read the designator out of the existing scope sentence at `spec-v0.2:115`, "anywhere in §3.3" | Needs the region to find the sentence and the sentence to find the region, so it must be broken by locating that sentence with a whole-document search for a longer prose phrase. That replaces one textual proxy with a **larger** one, which is the failure this family has committed four times. |
| **(E)** | hardcode `"### 3.3 "`, or the number `3.3`, in the validator | Two lines, and rejected on the R10 section's own argument, which condemned it in advance: a literal standing in for a document property breaks the moment the heading is reworded or renumbered, and it makes the docstring's "no heading text, no section number and no sentence is hardcoded" false in a new place. It also cannot detect the renumbering it would break on. |

**(F) was taken:** the specification declares its own scope designator in the marker sentence, and the validator resolves it against the document. It is the smallest contract that carries an *identity* rather than a *position*, it hardcodes nothing in the validator, and it is the only one of the six in which a renumbered heading and an unrenumbered marker **disagree inside one document** and fail closed together. It also makes an existing sentence true rather than retreating to meet the code, which is the direction this bundle has taken since R7. Its cost is stated rather than hidden: the bundle now depends on one clause of specification prose that a reviewer must read, and it introduces one new failure mode — two headings for one declared section — which `NEG-R3B2-ar` pins.

**Verification.** Red before green over **byte-identical** witness bytes: each shape is built from the R13 specification and handed unchanged to the R12 candidate's validator and to this one, so nothing but the mechanism differs. Detection is the state of the three §3.3 checks, never the run's exit code — the convention this ledger has used since R6 Standards `S1R6-N04`, and it is load-bearing here, because on the R12 mechanism the run *is* red for the first three shapes while the defect is *undetected*: `NEG-R3B2-an` and `NEG-R3B2-ao` report "not caught", `NEG-R3B2-al`, `NEG-R3B2-am` and `POS-HEAD-b` report "inapplicable", and a reviewer reading only `EXIT=1` would conclude the opposite of the truth.

| Shape | Witness bytes | On the R12 mechanism | On these bytes |
|---|---|---|---|
| deeper subsection `#### 3.3.1` above the marker, rogue row at `spec-v0.2:96` | 70,243 B, 579 lines, `b8b9e5fc32d48e8c02f3edfffbe9fad5e1f961a4cc53de218085b074aacf0232` | all three §3.3 checks `PASS`, both printing `bus 6` while the section declares seven | both class checks `FAIL`: `carries a row for bus_statement outside the class table` |
| same-level subsection `### 3.3.1`, the document's own house style | 70,242 B, 579 lines, `ee704ae7eaec9441d8afda8e2deffdcee6cf25a62d327ca85aac20525d63988a` | all three `PASS`, `bus 6` | both class checks `FAIL`, same message |
| duplicate heading `### 3.3` restated | 70,242 B, 579 lines, `7199fe0e2ee9c0e297097e32e0f4b61ae8c4b4e971b0fd203513c19e766e143a` | all three `PASS`, `bus 6` | all three `FAIL`: `carries 2 unfenced headings for the declared section 3.3, and exactly one is required` |
| genuine sibling `### 3.4` carrying a complete class table — the control | 70,317 B, 585 lines, `bf203b42f877e55d1a79669406b541e6cd693faa2dbed146b255c0ec6d3fba4a` | all three `PASS` | all three `PASS`, unchanged — the widened start did not widen the end |
| the truthful bytes | 70,049 B, 579 lines, `f681acb7b486f2763517a7f56430611b45c95bad973115c4114240f3dcf1e457` | all three `PASS` | all three `PASS`; 57/0 positive, 93/0/0 fixtures, 12/0/0 controls, `EXIT=0` |

Additionally, the same three shapes were built from the **R11 specification**, without the anchoring clause, and run against the R12 candidate's own unmodified bundle: 70,149 B `8820e705451cdf152d9e303d28ff0b4147aef139797a1133a6d4d6a5f8efb6d8`, 70,148 B `ad6ff4ede8914c9f9e6ce108b5d3598c29927d6b1b0108d2f20c234415f9b1e5` and 70,148 B `5e9ba06192f372ca0524d3657ea2fa3247e64f6dca274ae8f0b9527357158b2c`, each at 579 lines, each reporting **57 positive checks run, 0 failed**. The blocker is therefore reproduced on the reviewed subject as shipped, not only on a subject this round constructed.

**Three negative fixtures and one control pin the family**, taking the suite from 90 to 93 fixtures and from 11 to 12 controls. `NEG-R3B2-ap` is the deeper-subsection form, `NEG-R3B2-aq` the same-level form and `NEG-R3B2-ar` the duplicate-designator form; all three are line-count preserving, so the mutated specification stays at 579 lines and no earlier fixture is rendered inapplicable by them. Against the R12 mechanism carrying this fixture set all three report "not caught". `POS-HEAD-c` is the load-bearing control and is the obligation the three fixtures create: a genuine sibling `### 3.4`, at §3.3's own level and carrying a complete class table declaring a seventh bus leading terminal, **must not** trip, so designs (A) and (D) catch every fixture above and fail here, as design (C) of the R10 round already failed at `POS-HEAD-a`. The `LEDGER_ANCHORS` table gains a twenty-sixth entry binding the new clause at `spec-v0.2:103` to its text, because a clause the region reader depends on is load-bearing in the strongest sense this bundle has: delete it and all three §3.3 checks fail closed.

**What this does not establish.** One residual is **created** here and disclosed rather than hidden: the region's identity now rests on one clause of prose at `spec-v0.2:103`, and nothing binds the *wording* of that clause to the heading it names beyond the twenty-sixth `LEDGER_ANCHORS` entry, which checks that the line contains the text and not that the text is true. A designator written in a form the pattern does not read — a Unicode section sign other than `§`, a spelled-out "section 3.3", a designator carried in the heading only — fails closed, which is the safe direction, but it is a false red on a document a reader would accept. The `§` form is not defended by any check. The setext residual, the block-quoted and list-item fence residual, the HTML-block residual and the pipe-less degenerate-row residual are all unchanged and unaddressed. The widening of `SPEC_ENUMERATES_ALL_CLASS_TERMINALS` disclosed under the R10 Standards section is unchanged and is now slightly wider again, since the prose prefix it may satisfy itself from is reliably in the region. The `BUS_VERBS` / `LEDGER_TERMINALS` / `FRAME_TERMINALS` constants remain a third copy (`S1R4-N07`); a default run still does not hash the validator's own bytes (`S1R4-N02`); the two EBNF readers still disagree on nested comments; `COPYRIGHT_GATE_PRESERVED` still binds neither the text of the preserved notice, nor the pinned artifact digests, nor the eighteen upstream source identities (`S1R3-N04`). This revision touched none of them. It establishes no verdict, no acceptance, no freshness and no authority: **S1 remains `Pending`, M2–M7 remain `Absent`, and the bundle remains NOT INTEGRATED**. The R1–R12 verdicts each remain valid over their own subject and none is superseded.

## S1R12-B01 (Spec axis) — the change ledger stated a CRLF count its own captured output contradicted

**Old.** The `S1R10-B01 (Spec axis)` section above states the per-file line-ending census in two places — its `**New.**` paragraph and its `**Verification.**` paragraph — and both said the captured validator output carries **200** CRLF pairs and no bare LF. Measured over the R11 bytes, `gaia-s1-r2-validator-output.txt` carried **206**:

| Artifact | Claimed | Measured over `596224b2…` |
|---|---:|---:|
| change ledger, `S1R10-B01 (Spec axis)` **New.** | 200 | 206 |
| change ledger, `S1R10-B01 (Spec axis)` **Verification.** | 200 | 206 |
| bundle manifest §6 | 206 | 206 |

So the bundle contradicted itself in two directions at once: the ledger disagreed with the file it describes, and it disagreed with the manifest describing the same file. The manifest was right. The number is not decorative — it is the *witness* of a repair whose entire subject is a file asserting something false about its own bytes, and the Verification paragraph carrying it is the paragraph that certifies the measurement was taken. A stale witness inside a "measurement, not mutation" paragraph is the same defect class that paragraph exists to close, one file over. `200` was the count over the R9 output; the R11 round added four fixtures and two controls, which added six printed lines, and re-stamped the manifest for the new value while leaving the ledger on the old one.

**New.** Both claims state the count measured over the output file this bundle ships, and both name the correction and the round that made it, so a reviewer diffing against the R11 ledger sees a change stated as a change rather than a silent renumber. The figure moves again this round for the same mechanical reason it moved at R11 — three fixtures and one control add four printed lines — so it is re-derived from the shipped file rather than carried forward from either previous value, and manifest §6 is re-derived from the same read in the same pass.

**Rationale — three designs were compared.** *(A)* correct the two ledger figures to the measured count. *(B)* delete the count from both ledger paragraphs and cite manifest §6 instead, so the number exists in one place. *(C)* add a validator check binding the ledger's and the manifest's line-ending prose to the measured bytes. (B) removes the duplication that caused the drift and is genuinely tempting, and it was rejected: the Verification paragraph's job is to record what *this lane measured*, and a Verification paragraph that cites another file's number has stopped being a measurement record — the R10 Spec blocker exists precisely because an unverified claim was inherited rather than measured. (C) is the real fix for the class and is **out of scope for this round**: it is a new mechanism binding a manifest's and a ledger's prose to their own bytes, the R10 Spec section already disclosed its absence as an open residual, and adding a check on a repair round that was authorized for two named blockers is the kind of scope widening this bundle refuses elsewhere. (A) was taken, with the drift-producing coupling named in the text so the next round can see it before it re-stamps. The residual (C) would close is restated below, unchanged, as open.

**Verification.** Measurement, not mutation, on both sides — the claim under test is a statement about bytes, so the witness is the byte count itself. Over the R12 subject `596224b2…`, `open(out,'rb').read().count(b'\r\n')` returns **206** and `.count(b'\n') - .count(b'\r\n')` returns **0**, against two ledger paragraphs asserting 200 and a manifest §6 asserting 206; the ledger contained the string `200 of them` once and `at 200 CRLF` once, and `206` zero times. Over these bytes the same two measurements return **210** and **0**, the ledger contains `200` in neither claim, and the two ledger paragraphs, manifest §6 and the shipped file agree on one number, reproduced by a single read across all fourteen files: thirteen at 0 CR, one — the captured output — at 210 CRLF and 0 bare LF. No positive check changed, no fixture was added and none was removed for this group, because there is still no mechanism here to pin; the three fixtures and one control this round adds belong to the Standards group above. Every check name, fixture identifier and control identifier newly cited in this file resolves, which is what `LEDGER_NAMES_RESOLVE` decides on every run, and the coupled paragraph-count constant moved from 19 to 21 in the same edit as the two sections it counts: with the sections added and the constant left at 19 the check reports `FAIL … found 21` and the run exits 1, which is the red state, and with both moved it reports `PASS`.

**What this does not establish.** Nothing mechanical now prevents this recurring, and this round is the second consecutive demonstration that it will: the manifest and the change ledger are the two artifacts in the bundle whose self-description no check reads, `--verify-manifest` still binds only the inventory rows of the other thirteen files, and the count corrected here is the same count that will drift the moment a future round adds a fixture and re-stamps one file but not the other. The residual recorded under the R10 Spec section — that no check binds a manifest's prose to a manifest's bytes — is unchanged, and this section extends it to the ledger by demonstration. `S1R3-N05(b)` remains closed as a *nuance* and not as a *mechanism*. It establishes no verdict, no acceptance, no freshness and no authority: **S1 remains `Pending`, M2–M7 remain `Absent`, and the bundle remains NOT INTEGRATED**.

## S1R14-B01 (Standards axis) — the §3.3 region ended the section at a heading that is its own descendant

The R14 Standards review returned `REQUEST_CHANGES` over subject `b219cfff1135575ed1ebd3d46a4049cfe0cff52adbdad76c59a0a0e8de8b00fd` (internal thirteen-file digest `b2a2ecda6ef4459897845e24098a4fb03c0f6382c6533730d0eec5a23cd24790`, 14 files, 583,299 bytes) on one blocker, and this lane reproduced it independently, from the shipped bytes and before any edit was made. **The two R14 axes number their first blocker alike and mean different things**, for the third consecutive review pair: the Standards `S1R14-B01` is this validator defect, the Spec `S1R14-B01` is a stale anchor count in the specification, and this ledger cites the axis with the identifier throughout. They are repaired as separate groups because they are separate defects in separate files.

**Old.** The R13 repair replaced the last proxy at the region's *opening* boundary and said, in the docstring and in the `S1R12-B01 (Standards axis)` section above, that **"the closing boundary is untouched, deliberately"**. It was, and that is the defect. `declared_section_region` came out of R13 holding two incompatible readings of the same document at its two ends:

- the **opening** scan resolves the declared designator `3.3` against `^ {0,3}(#{1,6})[ \t]+3\.3\.?(?![\d.])`, which deliberately does **not** match `### 3.3.1`. Its own docstring states the reason: "a deeper subsection is therefore *inside* the region rather than the start of it, which is what a reader of `### 7.1.1` already assumes";
- the **closing** scan asked one question — is this unfenced heading at the declared level or shallower — and for `### 3.3.1` answered yes, ending §3.3 four lines into itself.

So the reader treated `### 3.3.1` as a descendant when deciding where §3.3 *starts* and as a stranger when deciding where it *stops*. The R12 section above had already established, and this specification's own `### 7.1.1` beneath `### 7.1` at `spec-v0.2:305` and `spec-v0.2:283` already demonstrates, that in this document the **numbering** and not the ATX level carries the nesting — the argument was made, accepted, and then applied at one end only.

The witness is the seventh-verb row this family has used since R10, `| `bus_statement` | `promote`, … | 7 | …`, placed past the class table in §3.3's closing prose with a same-level `### 3.3.1` heading two lines above it. Both edits replace a blank line, so the specification stays at **579** lines and no citation and no `LEDGER_ANCHORS` entry drifts. Measured over the R14 bytes the region ran **8,260 characters and 39 lines** where §3.3 ran **10,277 and 44**: the last five lines of the section, the rogue declaration among them, were read by none of the three §3.3 checks, and all three reported `PASS` with both class checks printing **`bus 6`** while the section in front of the reviewer declared seven. The identical row with the subsection heading removed is caught by both class checks on the same mechanism, so **placement alone decided detection** — for the eighth consecutive round, and for the fourth time in this one function.

**New.** The closing scan is taught the reading the opening scan already had. A heading at the declared level or shallower still ends the region **unless its own designator is a proper descendant of the declared one**, decided by the same `number` the marker sentence at `spec-v0.2:103` declares and the same `re.escape` of it the opening anchor uses: `^ {0,3}#{1,6}[ \t]+` + `3\.3` + `\.\d`. `### 3.3.1` and `### 3.3.10.2` are stepped over. `### 3.4`, `### 3.30` and `## 4.` are not — a proper descendant must carry the declared designator followed by a dot **and** a digit, so a shared string prefix is not a descendant, which is the hazard the predicate introduces and the reason it is spelled `\.\d` rather than as a prefix test. A heading carrying no designator at all is untouched by the predicate and is still decided by level alone, so a legitimate `#### Notes` inside §3.3 stays inside it and a decoy `#### ` heading still cannot truncate the section, which is what `NEG-R3B2-ai` pins. One predicate, one scan, no second traversal of the document and no new input.

**No specification bytes are required by this repair.** The clause the reader depends on, `spec-v0.2:103`, is the one R13 added and `LEDGER_ANCHORS` already binds twice; this round reads one more property out of the designator it already carries. The specification is edited in this bundle for the three Spec blockers below, not for this one, and none of those edits adds or removes a line.

**Rationale — six designs were compared, four of them seriously.**

| | Design | Why not |
|---|---|---|
| **(A)** | stop only at a **strictly shallower** heading — climb the level test by one | Closes `### 3.3.1` and breaks the sibling. `### 3.4` is at §3.3's own level, so §3.3 would then run through §3.4 to `## 4.`, and a class table in §3.4 would be read as a §3.3 defect. `POS-HEAD-c` and `POS-HEAD-d` both fail. It is also unsound *for this document* for the same reason (B) of the R12 round was: level does not encode nesting here. |
| **(B)** | stop at the first heading whose designator is **not** a proper descendant, ignoring level entirely | Catches the fixture and reopens S1R8-B01 from the other side: a legitimate deeper heading carrying no designator — `#### Notes`, or the `#### a decoy sub-heading` of `NEG-R3B2-ai` — is not a descendant, so it would end the region. That is the "nearest excuse to stop" the R8 repair removed, re-armed under a new name. |
| **(C)** | order every designator in the document and stop at the first **sibling or ancestor** of the declared one | (B) with more machinery, and it fails closed on exactly the sections that carry no designator, which this document has. It also needs a whole-document designator pass the reader does not otherwise make, which is the broad scan this family has refused since R7. |
| **(D)** | have the specification declare the section's **end** as well as its start — a second marker sentence | A second prose contract to keep in sync with the first, and rejected on the R13 section's own argument against replacing one textual proxy with a larger one. It also doubles the surface a renumbering can desynchronize while adding no detection the designator does not already carry. |
| **(E)** | hardcode the terminator — `"## 4. "`, or §3.3's known extent | Rejected on the standing argument of the R10 and R12 sections, which condemned it in advance: a literal standing in for a document property breaks the moment the document is reworded or renumbered, and cannot detect the renumbering it breaks on. |
| **(F)** | suppress the whole level test and read §3.3 to the end of the file | Catches every fixture in the family and fails `POS-FENCE-c`, `POS-HEAD-a`, `POS-HEAD-c` and `POS-HEAD-d`. `spec-v0.2:115` says "anywhere in §3.3", not anywhere in the document. This is design (C) of the R10 round for the third time. |

**The descendant-designator exemption was taken.** It is the smallest change that makes the two ends of one reader agree: the property it tests — "is this heading numbered as a descendant of the declared section" — is the property the opening anchor already tests with the sign reversed, derived from the same declared designator, with nothing hardcoded and no second pass over the document. Its cost is stated rather than hidden: the reader now over-reads, not under-reads, when a document numbers an unrelated section as a descendant of §3.3 — a renumbered `### 3.3.9` in place of `## 4.` would be read as part of §3.3 — which raises a false red rather than hiding a declaration, and is the direction this reader has chosen every time it is unsure.

**Verification.** Red before green over **byte-identical** witness bytes: each shape is built once from the R14 specification and handed unchanged to the R14 candidate's validator and to this one, so nothing but the mechanism differs. Detection is the state of the three §3.3 checks, never the run's exit code — the convention this ledger has used since R6 Standards `S1R6-N04`, and it is load-bearing here for a reason this round measured rather than assumed. The witness bytes are line-count preserving at 579 lines, so the specification stays at its shipped length, every line citation and every load-bearing anchor resolves unchanged over them, and **no earlier fixture is rendered inapplicable**. A whole-suite replay over a witness is nevertheless *not* a clean run and must not be read as one: a fixture consumes its own text anchor, so over the `NEG-R3B2-as` witness that fixture and `POS-HEAD-d` both report `INAPP`, and the eight other §3.3 controls report `FAIL` because a control mutates elsewhere in a document that already carries the defect. Measured over these bytes that replay reports 57 positive checks with 2 failed, 94 fixtures with 0 not caught and 1 inapplicable, and 13 controls with 8 falsely tripped and 1 inapplicable, at exit 1 — a red run whose red is the *base* document, not the control. A reviewer reading the exit code alone would draw the wrong conclusion in both directions, which is exactly why detection is read from the three §3.3 checks.

| Shape | Witness bytes | On the R14 mechanism | On these bytes |
|---|---|---|---|
| same-level `### 3.3.1` past the marker, rogue row two lines behind it — `NEG-R3B2-as` | 70,242 B, 579 lines, `1653473b91cc1cd1e1ce9a8570e61cdb8afb1f590a1415348d908c7d6ff61e1a` | region 8,260 chars / 39 lines, rogue row **outside** it; all three §3.3 checks `PASS`, both class checks printing `bus 6` while the section declares seven | region 10,277 chars / 44 lines, rogue row **inside** it; both class checks `FAIL`: `section 3.3 carries a row for bus_statement outside the class table` |
| genuine sibling `### 3.4` at the same two seams — `POS-HEAD-d` | 70,239 B, 579 lines, `ed635c9e46cc870cf6a2da1d2853cd15f82bd3c58b8f239a7e935411fc47e0db` | region 8,260 chars, all three `PASS` | region 8,260 chars, all three `PASS`, unchanged — the widened end did not widen past the sibling |
| the same rogue row with the subsection heading **removed** | — | region 10,227 chars, both class checks `FAIL` — placement alone decided detection | both class checks `FAIL`, unchanged |
| the truthful bytes | 70,049 B, 579 lines, `f681acb7b486f2763517a7f56430611b45c95bad973115c4114240f3dcf1e457` | all three `PASS`; 57/0 positive, 93/0/0 fixtures, 12/0/0 controls | all three `PASS` |

**One negative fixture and one control pin the family**, taking the suite from 93 to **94** fixtures and from 12 to **13** controls, with no positive check added and none removed. `NEG-R3B2-as` is the same-level descendant form; `POS-HEAD-d` is the obligation it creates and is the *same mutation at the same two seams with the heading's designator changed*, so the pair differs in one thing only and design (A) above catches the fixture and fails the control. The deeper `#### 3.3.1` form needs no fixture: level 4 is already below the declared level 3 and never terminated the region, which `NEG-R3B2-ap` establishes from the opening side. No `LEDGER_ANCHORS` entry is added, because this repair reads a property of a designator the table already binds; the count stands at **26** and is restated truthfully in `spec-v0.2:571` by the Spec group below. Every check name, fixture identifier and control identifier newly cited in this file resolves, which `LEDGER_NAMES_RESOLVE` decides on every run, and the coupled paragraph-count constant moved from 21 to 25 in the same edit as the four sections it counts: with the sections added and the constant left at 21 that check reports `FAIL … found 25` and the run exits 1, which is the red state, and with both moved it reports `PASS`.

**What this does not establish.** The residual this repair **creates** is disclosed: an unrelated section renumbered as a descendant of §3.3 is read as part of §3.3, a false red on a document a reviewer might accept, and nothing binds the numbering of §4 to its not being a subsection of §3.3. The residual the R13 round created is unchanged — the region's identity rests on one clause of prose at `spec-v0.2:103`, and the twenty-sixth `LEDGER_ANCHORS` entry checks that the line contains that text, not that the text is true — and the `§` designator form is still defended by no check. The setext residual, the block-quoted and list-item fence residual, the HTML-block residual and the pipe-less degenerate-row residual are all unchanged and unaddressed. The `BUS_VERBS` / `LEDGER_TERMINALS` / `FRAME_TERMINALS` constants remain a third copy (`S1R4-N07`); a default run still does not hash the validator's own bytes (`S1R4-N02`); the two EBNF readers still disagree on nested comments; `COPYRIGHT_GATE_PRESERVED` still binds neither the text of the preserved notice, nor the pinned artifact digests, nor the eighteen upstream source identities (`S1R3-N04`). **Eight consecutive rounds have found the next escape in this one function, each a notch further out than the last**; that this round found the far boundary after R13 found the near one is evidence that the ninth exists, not that the family is closed. It establishes no verdict, no acceptance, no freshness and no authority: **S1 remains `Pending`, M2–M7 remain `Absent`, and the bundle remains NOT INTEGRATED**. The R1–R14 verdicts each remain valid over their own subject and none is superseded.

## S1R14-B01 (Spec axis) — the specification stated twenty-five load-bearing anchors against a table of twenty-six

**Old.** `spec-v0.2:571` said `LEDGER_ANCHORS_RESOLVE` "asserts that twenty-five load-bearing citations resolve to a line *containing the claimed text* (sixteen at R3, nine added at R4 for the claims this revision rests on)". Sixteen plus nine is twenty-five and the parenthesis was internally consistent, which is why it survived: it was true of the R4 bundle and was never re-derived. The R13 round added a twenty-sixth entry — the second `spec-v0.2:103` anchor binding the §3.3 scope clause the region reader depends on — and said so in its own `S1R12-B01 (Standards axis)` section above, in the manifest §4 row for the specification, and in the captured run, which prints `all 26 load-bearing citations resolve to a line containing the claimed text` on every execution. The specification alone was left at twenty-five. The same sentence also bounded the ledger's citations as "not all seventy-odd", against **167** on the same bytes, a figure `LEDGER_LINE_REFS_IN_RANGE` also prints on every run.

| Artifact | Claimed | Measured over `b219cfff…` |
|---|---:|---:|
| specification `spec-v0.2:571`, anchor count | 25 | 26 |
| specification `spec-v0.2:571`, ledger citation count | "seventy-odd" | 167 |
| `LEDGER_ANCHORS` table in the validator | — | 26 |
| captured validator output | — | 26 anchors, 167 citations |
| manifest §4, specification row | — | 26 anchors, 167 citations |

So the bundle contradicted itself in the same shape the R12 Spec blocker had: a figure duplicated into prose, moved in three places and left in a fourth. The number is not decorative — the sentence carrying it is the one that discloses the anchor table as *author-selected and partial*, so understating its size understates the coverage a reviewer is being asked to accept as incomplete, in a paragraph whose whole purpose is to be honest about that incompleteness.

**New.** Both figures state what the shipped run prints, the provenance is re-derived rather than carried forward — sixteen at R3, nine at R4, one at R13, twenty-six in total — and the correction is recorded *as* a correction, with the round that made each figure stale named, so a reviewer diffing against the R14 specification sees a change stated as a change rather than a silent renumber. The citation figure is re-measured over **these** bytes after the four sections of this round were written, since writing them changes it.

**Rationale — three designs were compared.** *(A)* correct both figures to the measured counts and name the drift. *(B)* delete both figures from the specification and cite the captured output instead, so each number exists in one place. *(C)* add a validator check binding the specification's stated figures to the measured ones. (B) removes the duplication that caused the drift and was rejected for the reason the R13 round rejected its own (B): this paragraph's job is to disclose a *limit* of the anchor table, and a disclosure that defers its own magnitude to another file has stopped disclosing. (C) is the real fix for the class and is **out of scope**: it is a new mechanism binding a document's prose to a measurement, the R12 Spec section already disclosed its absence as an open residual, and adding a check on a round authorized for four named blockers is the scope widening this bundle refuses elsewhere. (A) was taken, with the coupling named in the text so the next round sees it before it re-stamps.

**Verification.** Measurement, not mutation — the claim under test is a statement about a count, so the witness is the count. Over the R14 subject `b219cfff…` the validator's own anchor table holds **26** entries and its captured output prints `all 26 load-bearing citations` and `all 167 line citations`, against a specification sentence asserting twenty-five and "seventy-odd"; the specification contained the string `twenty-five load-bearing` once and `seventy-odd` once, and `26` and `167` zero times in that sentence. Over these bytes the same two measurements are reproduced by the run that ships with this bundle, the specification names both, and the specification, the manifest §4 specification row, the validator's table and the captured output agree. No positive check changed, no fixture was added and none was removed for this group; the one fixture and one control this round adds belong to the Standards group above. This edit changes the text of specification lines in place and adds no line and removes none, so the file stands at **579** lines and every `spec-v0.2:` citation and every load-bearing anchor resolves unchanged, which `LEDGER_LINE_REFS_IN_RANGE` and `LEDGER_ANCHORS_RESOLVE` decide on every run.

**What this does not establish.** Nothing mechanical prevents this recurring, and this is the third consecutive round in which a figure duplicated into prose drifted from the bytes it describes — 200 CRLF at R12, twenty-five anchors here. The specification, the manifest and this ledger are the three artifacts whose self-description no check reads; `--verify-manifest` still binds only the inventory rows of the other thirteen files. The anchor table itself is unchanged and remains **author-selected and partial**, which is what the corrected sentence continues to say: it covers the citations that carry the argument, not all 167, and a future edit can still reintroduce the defect class outside the anchored set. It establishes no verdict, no acceptance, no freshness and no authority: **S1 remains `Pending`, M2–M7 remain `Absent`, and the bundle remains NOT INTEGRATED**.

## S1R14-B02 (Spec axis) — the residual-uncertainty section reported the R6 suite and one control family as the whole

**Old.** `spec-v0.2:574` ended with **"The shipped suite is 57 positive checks, 62 negative fixtures and 4 disclosed-boundary positive controls."** That was the R6 suite. Measured over the R14 subject the shipped suite was **57 positive checks, 93 negative fixtures and 12 disclosed-boundary positive controls**, so two of the three figures had been stale for four rounds while the sentence containing them presents itself as the record of how strongly the repair was tested. `spec-v0.2:573` compounded it from the other side: it names "four disclosed-boundary positive controls (`POS-FIELD-a`..`POS-FIELD-d`)", which is a true statement about the *field-position family* and was read by the following sentence as a statement about the control set.

| Artifact | Claimed | Measured over `b219cfff…` | Shipped here |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| `spec-v0.2:574`, positive checks | 57 | 57 | 57 |
| `spec-v0.2:574`, negative fixtures | 62 | 93 | 94 |
| `spec-v0.2:574`, positive controls | 4 | 12 | 13 |
| control families named anywhere in §15 | the field-position family only | four families | four families |

The families the R14 subject actually carried were `POS-FIELD-a`..`-d` (4), `POS-PIPELESS-a` (1), `POS-FENCE-a`..`-d` (4) and `POS-HEAD-a`..`-c` (3). A reviewer reading §15 to decide how much mutation pressure the repair had been under would have been told 62 and 4 against 93 and 12, and would have found no mention of three of the four families that carry the §3.3 boundary work — which is the work the last five rounds of blockers are about.

**New.** `spec-v0.2:574` states the three figures the captured run prints over **these** bytes — 57, 94 and 13 — declares them re-derived each round rather than carried forward, and names both the stale value and the round it belonged to. `spec-v0.2:573` now enumerates all four control families and what each one bounds, and says explicitly that the four `POS-FIELD-a`..`POS-FIELD-d` controls are the field-position family and not the whole set. The figures are written after the final bytes settle, because the fixture and control this round adds change two of them.

**Rationale — three designs were compared.** *(A)* restate the figures and enumerate the families in place. *(B)* remove the figures from §15 and point at the captured output. *(C)* add a check binding §15's stated suite figures to `len(CHECKS)`, `len(FIXTURES)` and `len(PRESERVED)`. (C) is genuinely attractive here — unlike the anchor count and the CRLF census, these three numbers are already computed by the running program, so the check is three comparisons and no new reader — and it was still rejected, for scope: this round is authorized for four named blockers, a new positive check is new mechanism, and adding one under a repair mandate is what this bundle has refused at R12 and again above. It is recorded below as the mechanism that would close the class, so the next round can adopt it deliberately rather than discover it. (B) was rejected for the reason (B) is always rejected here: the sentence's purpose is to state how hard the author tested this revision, and a claim of rigour that defers its own magnitude has stopped being one. (A) was taken.

**Verification.** Measurement, not mutation. Over the R14 subject `b219cfff…` the validator defined 57 checks, 93 fixtures and 12 controls, and its captured output printed `positive checks:   57 run, 0 failed`, `negative fixtures: 93 run, 0 not caught, 0 inapplicable` and `boundary controls: 12 run, 0 falsely tripped, 0 inapplicable`, against a specification sentence asserting 57, 62 and 4; the four control families were field-position ×4, pipe-less ×1, fenced-block ×4 and heading-boundary ×3, and §15 named one of them. Over these bytes the same three counts are 57, 94 and 13, the families are field-position ×4, pipe-less ×1, fenced-block ×4 and heading-boundary ×4, the specification names all four with their bounds, and the specification and the captured output agree on every figure. Both edits change the text of specification lines in place and add no line and remove none, so the file stands at **579** lines and no citation and no anchor drifts.

**What this does not establish.** No check reads these three figures, so nothing stops the next round re-stamping the validator and forgetting §15 exactly as the R7 through R13 rounds did. The mechanism that would close it is named above and deliberately not built here. The suite figures also say nothing about suite *quality*: 94 fixtures and 13 controls is a count of mutations the author wrote, and eight consecutive rounds have shown that the mutation the author did not write is the one that matters. It establishes no verdict, no acceptance, no freshness and no authority: **S1 remains `Pending`, M2–M7 remain `Absent`, and the bundle remains NOT INTEGRATED**.

## S1R14-B03 (Spec axis) — the revision block and the S1 gate row still identified the candidate as R4

**Old.** `spec-v0.2:10` opened **"This is the R4 repair of the R3 candidate"**; `spec-v0.2:18` said "Repairs in this revision: … plus `S1R3-B01` and `S1R3-B02`" and described "the R4 repair"; the S1 gate row at `spec-v0.2:474` read **"Pending — the R1, R2 and R3 reviews all returned `REQUEST_CHANGES`; this bundle is the R4 candidate and is unreviewed"**; and `spec-v0.2:484` told the next reviewer to test "the two R4 repairs" and to treat "the R4 repair's own claim" with suspicion. The bundle around those sentences was the R13 repair of the R14 candidate's predecessor, carrying eleven rounds of repairs and bound by ten independent reviews. The specification named three of them.

This is the same defect class as `S1R10-B02` — a document re-stamped in some places and left carrying old claims in others — and the same class as the change ledger header that was stale from R7 to R10. It matters more here than in either: the revision block and the gate row are the two places a reviewer looks to learn **which subject they are being asked to bind and what has already been decided about its predecessors**, and both were understating the review history by eight rounds. A reviewer who trusted `spec-v0.2:474` would have believed three prior reviews existed where eleven subjects had in fact been reviewed and had all returned `REQUEST_CHANGES`.

**New.** `spec-v0.2:10` identifies this bundle as the **R15 repair of the R14 candidate**, names the round-versus-bundle offset that has held since R10, and points at the manifest for the fixed point. The `**S1 relationship.**` block keeps the R1, R2 and R3 paragraphs verbatim — they are the record of those three subjects and are not this round's to rewrite — and the exact lineage from R4 onward is added to the end of the R3 paragraph in place: each subject, its ordinal aggregate digest, and the blocking findings it returned, ending with the R14 candidate at `b219cfff1135575ed1ebd3d46a4049cfe0cff52adbdad76c59a0a0e8de8b00fd`, which is the direct entry subject of this revision. `spec-v0.2:18` names the four repairs this round owes and states that the R15 repair adds no bus verb, lattice, refusal code, authority or subsystem. `spec-v0.2:474` states eleven reviewed subjects, R1 through R14, all `REQUEST_CHANGES`, and this bundle as the unreviewed R15 repair. `spec-v0.2:484` names the four repairs a fresh review must test and replaces the R3 reviewer's spent probe suggestion with the one the R14 round earned.

**Nothing here implies approval, and the stampings that must not move did not move.** `**Status:** consolidated specification candidate; research and design only`, `**Milestone:** M1 established; M2-M5 absent; **NOT INTEGRATED**` and `**Authority:** advisory` are byte-identical. Every gate row other than S1 is byte-identical: M2 through M7 all still read `Absent`, and S1 still reads `Pending`. The word `REQUEST_CHANGES` appears in the new lineage eleven times and the word `APPROVE` appears nowhere in it. "It inherits no approval", "requires a fresh independent exact Standards + Spec review" and "its author grants no approval to it" are preserved, and `NO_SELF_APPROVAL`, `MILESTONE_MARKER`, `GATE_TABLE_M2_M5_ABSENT` and `R1_VERDICT_NOT_SUPERSEDED` each read these bytes on every run.

**Rationale — three designs were compared.** *(A)* re-stamp the four sentences in place and add the lineage inside the existing R3 paragraph. *(B)* add a new `**Review lineage.**` block with a table, which is how the manifest and this ledger carry the same information. *(C)* re-stamp only the two artifacts the blocker names — the revision block and the gate row — and leave `spec-v0.2:18` and `spec-v0.2:484` on R4. (B) is the more readable rendering and was rejected on cost: a table adds twelve lines to the specification, every `spec-v0.2:` citation below line 16 shifts, and all 26 `LEDGER_ANCHORS` entries and all of this file's line citations would need a mechanical remap — a large, purely incidental risk on a round whose Standards repair must be reviewable line by line. This bundle has kept the specification line-count stable deliberately since R6 for exactly that reason. (C) is the narrower reading of the blocker and was rejected because it manufactures a *new* untruth: with `spec-v0.2:10` restamped to R15 and `spec-v0.2:18` still describing "the R4 repair", the document contradicts itself eight lines apart, which is the defect this group exists to remove. (A) was taken: four sentences edited in place, no line added, no line removed.

**Verification.** Measurement, not mutation, plus the four bundle gates that read these exact sentences. Over the R14 subject `b219cfff…` the specification contained `This is the **R4 repair**` once, `this bundle is the R4 candidate and is unreviewed` once, and `R14` zero times; over these bytes it contains `This is the **R15 repair** of the R14 candidate` once, `this bundle is the R15 repair of the R14 candidate and is unreviewed` once, and the eight ordinal aggregate digests of the R4 through R14 subjects once each. The four edits change the text of specification lines in place and add no line and remove none, so the file stands at **579** lines, `LEDGER_LINE_REFS_IN_RANGE` resolves every citation against the same bounds, and `LEDGER_ANCHORS_RESOLVE` resolves all 26 anchors against unchanged line numbers — including `spec-v0.2:463`, `spec-v0.2:464`, `spec-v0.2:465` and `spec-v0.2:466`, which sit in §11 between the two edited regions of §12 and would be the first to move if a line had been added. `MILESTONE_MARKER` reads `M1 established; M2-M5 absent` unchanged, `GATE_TABLE_M2_M5_ABSENT` reads the untouched `Absent` rows, `NO_SELF_APPROVAL` reads `does not self-approve` unchanged, and `R1_VERDICT_NOT_SUPERSEDED` reads the unchanged R1 paragraph; all four `PASS` here and their fixtures `NEG-M-a`, `NEG-M-b` and `NEG-S-a` are each still caught.

**What this does not establish.** No check binds the revision block, the gate row or the lineage to anything: `MILESTONE_MARKER` and `GATE_TABLE_M2_M5_ABSENT` read the milestone and the M-rows, and nothing reads the R-number, the digest list or the count of reviewed subjects. The same drift can therefore recur on the next round, and the lineage is now eleven entries of hand-maintained digests — a larger surface to keep true than the sentence it replaced, which is the cost of stating it. Six of those digests are **carried forward from the manifest and this ledger and were not re-measured by this lane**, which does not hold the R4 through R12 bytes; only the R14 entry was measured here, against the fourteen files this revision entered on. They are recorded as prior rounds' measurements, not as this one's. It establishes no verdict, no acceptance, no freshness and no authority: **S1 remains `Pending`, M2–M7 remain `Absent`, and the bundle remains NOT INTEGRATED**, and every one of the eleven verdicts listed remains valid over its own subject and none is superseded.
